answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work tied to a per-agent kernel: each identity must solve a unique cipher challenge derived from its own key, so forging N identities costs N independent computations rather than one shared effort. Answers are then gossiped across the island of peers, who verify the work before attesting. An attacker must burn real compute per fake identity, and the cipher binds each identity to its kernel, making mass forgery economically punitive. The Agent0208 deployment anchors trust at b2K4C4aLPS.
